mainTopic: When do כלי שרת make things holy at the wrong time? The cases are the night קמיצה and the late לחם הפנים. The amud then turns to washing hands after urinating in the מקדש.
overview: The גמרא asks why a מנחה whose קומץ was taken at night must be burned, instead of putting the handful back and redoing it by day. אבוה דרבי אבין explains that כלי שרת make their contents holy even at the wrong time. A ברייתא seems to contradict this, but the גמרא answers that wrong-time קדושה is enough to make the item פסול, though not enough to let it be offered. רבי זירא then challenges from the לחם הפנים: bread placed on the שולחן after שבת is simply left until the next שבת, so why doesn't it become holy and פסול? רבא answers that placing something the night before is not 'too early', but placing it a full day or more before is, so the Sunday bread never becomes holy. When the גמרא asks why the bread doesn't become holy once Friday night arrives, רבינא says it was removed before nightfall. מר זוטרא says an improper arrangement is like one done by a monkey. Finally, the גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה and asks why someone who urinates must wash his hands. רבי אבא begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not return the handful and redo it by day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a קומץ taken at night must be burned. Why not put it back into the מנחה and take a fresh handful in the daytime?
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us put it back, and then take the handful again in the daytime!
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier, אבוה דרבי אבין taught that if a כהן took the קומץ from a מנחה at night, the מנחה must be burned. The גמרא now asks why it can't simply be fixed by putting the handful back and redoing the קמיצה by day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption behind the question is that a קמיצה done at the wrong time simply doesn't count. If it doesn't count, the flour should still be ordinary מנחה flour that can be mixed back in. The harsh ruling of burning seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: let us return it (put the handful back)
let us take a handful (do קמיצה) from it
the כהן's act of taking a handful of flour from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This line has no stated subject. It refers back to the previous discussion about a קמיצה done at night (before dawn), which אבוה דרבי אבין ruled must be burned.

phrases.english: Let us return it, and then again
phrases.notes: Put the handful back into the rest of the מנחה.

phrases.english: take a handful from it by day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling (earlier) that a nighttime קמיצה requires burning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling of אבוה דרבי אבין that the מנחה must be burned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the nighttime קמיצה is invalid, it can simply be undone and redone properly, so burning is unnecessary.

steps.title: Service vessels sanctify even at the wrong time
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דרבי אבין explains his own ruling: a כלי שרת makes its contents holy even when it is not the proper time. So the handful is already holy and cannot be returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He taught the ברייתא and he also gave its reason: service vessels make things holy even when it is not their proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same person who taught the ruling also explained it. Once the handful entered the holy כלי, it became holy, so it can no longer go back into the ordinary flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that a wrong-time קמיצה does nothing at all. The answer says it does do something: the כלי שרת gives the handful קדושה even at night. Since it is now holy but cannot be offered properly, it is stuck. It cannot be returned to the flour, so it must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: service vessels of the בית המקדש

keyTerms.term: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: he taught it and he (himself) explained it

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that כלי שרת sanctify even at the wrong time, is what the rest of this passage tests and challenges.

phrases.english: He taught it (the ruling)
and he himself stated its reason:
Service vessels sanctify
even not at its proper time.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא תָּנֵי לַהּ וְהוּא אָמַר לַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Introduces the underlying principle that explains the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A nighttime קמיצה is simply void, so the handful can be returned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלי שרת already made the handful holy, so it cannot be returned and must be burned.

steps.title: Challenge: daytime offerings become holy only by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: anything offered by day becomes holy by day. This implies it does not become holy at night, which contradicts אבוה דרבי אבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: This is the rule. Whatever is offered by day becomes holy by day. Whatever is offered at night becomes holy at night. Whatever is offered both by day and at night becomes holy both by day and at night. The ברייתא says that whatever is offered by day becomes holy by day. That means by day, yes; at night, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and draws an inference from it to challenge the idea that כלי שרת make things holy at the wrong time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קומץ of a מנחה is a daytime offering. The ברייתא implies that a daytime offering does not become holy in a כלי at night. If so, the nighttime handful never became holy, and it should be possible to return it, just as step 1 suggested.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from a תנאי source)
yes / no (used in drawing an inference)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: This is the rule:
anything offered by day is consecrated by day,
and anything offered at night is consecrated at night,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַקָּרֵב בֵּין בַּיּוֹם וּבֵין בַּלַּיְלָה —
phrases.english: and anything offered both by day and at night
is consecrated both by day and at night.
In any case, it teaches:
anything offered by day is consecrated by day,
by day, yes; at night, no!
phrases.notes: The inference that contradicts אבוה דרבי אבין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle stated in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that כלי שרת sanctify even not at their proper time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies a daytime offering cannot become holy at night, so a nighttime קומץ should not be holy.

steps.title: Holy enough to be disqualified, not to be offered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means that at night the item is not holy enough to be offered. It is still holy enough to become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is not holy enough to be offered, but it is holy enough to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אבוה דרבי אבין by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer splits קדושה into two levels. Full holiness lets the item go on the מזבח. Basic holiness means it can no longer return to ordinary status and can become פסול. At night the קומץ gets only the basic level, which is enough to stop it from being put back.
steps.whatToRemember: The answer at this stage (later limited by רבא in step 8): a כלי שרת at the wrong time gives קדושה that is enough to make the item פסול, though not enough to let it be offered.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is not consecrated to be offered,
but it is consecrated to be disqualified.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: distinguishes two levels of קדושה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Not holy at night means no קדושה at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not holy at night means only not fit to be offered; it is still holy enough to become פסול.

steps.title: רבי זירא cites the case of the late לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא opens a new challenge by quoting a משנה. If the לחם הפנים and the בזיכין were arranged after שבת, and the בזיכין were burned on the next שבת, the offering is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged: If the כהן arranged the bread and the frankincense cups after שבת, and then burned the frankincense on the next שבת, it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: This step is setting up a new challenge. רבי זירא begins quoting a משנה about the לחם הפנים. The actual attack comes at the end of the quote (step 7).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread must sit on the שולחן from שבת to שבת. If it was placed on Sunday, it stayed less than a full week, so it is פסול. The next lines of the משנה give the fix, and that fix is what creates the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: the showbread placed on the שולחן each שבת
cups of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
If he arranged the bread and the frankincense cups
after Shabbat,
and burned the frankincense on (the next) Shabbat
it is disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the principle of step 2, using a different source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that כלי שרת sanctify even not at their proper time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only; the attack is completed in step 7.

steps.title: The fix: leave the bread until next שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: to avoid the פסול, the כהן should leave the bread on the שולחן until the following שבת. Staying there extra days does no harm.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should he do? He should leave it for the following שבת. Even if it stays on the table for many days, that does not matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא continues quoting the משנה, which gives the remedy. This is still setup for the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן does not remove the bread. He leaves it on the שולחן until the next שבת, and then arranges the לחם הפנים properly at its correct time. The Sunday placement is treated as if it never had any effect: it did not ruin the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: the golden table in the היכל, which is itself a כלי שרת
there is nothing wrong with that

phrases.english: How should he proceed?
He should leave it for the following Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עָמְדָה עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן יָמִים רַבִּים —
phrases.english: For even if it stood on the table many days
there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה begun in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread placed after שבת is not removed. It is left on the שולחן until the following שבת, when it is arranged properly. The early placement causes no harm.

steps.title: Why doesn't the bread become holy and disqualified?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks: the שולחן is a כלי שרת. Placing the bread there on Sunday should make it holy even though it is the wrong time, and then it should become פסול. So why does leaving it work?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? It should become holy and then become disqualified!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual attack. The משנה's remedy seems to contradict the principle that כלי שרת sanctify even at the wrong time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to steps 2 and 4, the שולחן should give the bread enough קדושה to become פסול, even on Sunday. The משנה instead treats the bread as untouched until the proper time. That suggests a כלי שרת does not sanctify at the wrong time.

keyTerms.meaning: let it become holy and become disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with the earlier answer. Step 4 said wrong-time קדושה is 'holy enough to become פסול'. רבי זירא uses exactly that idea against it: if so, the bread should be ruined, but the משנה says it is fine.

phrases.english: But why? Let it be consecrated and disqualified!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradiction from the משנה quoted in steps 5-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle that כלי שרת sanctify even not at their proper time, enough to become פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שולחן should have sanctified the Sunday bread and then made it פסול. Yet the משנה lets it stay and become valid.

steps.title: רבא: Night is not too early, but a day earlier is
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי זירא's question is a good one. He also says אבוה דרבי אבין is quoting a real ברייתא. The way out: placing something at night is not considered 'too early' (מחוסר זמן), but placing it a whole day early is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The one who asks, asks well. And אבוה דרבי אבין is also quoting a ברייתא. And the ברייתא holds: night is not 'lacking time', but a day earlier is 'lacking time'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רבי זירא's challenge by keeping both sources and drawing a line between them. Night-before placement makes the item holy, but day-before placement does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The night before a day counts as part of that day, so bread placed on the שולחן that night is not 'early' and the כלי שרת makes it holy. That is why it can become פסול. Bread placed on Sunday is a whole six days early, so the שולחן does not make it holy at all. That is why the משנה can tell the כהן to just leave it there until the next שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה)
'lacking time': done too early, before its proper time
he holds / is of the opinion

steps.whatToRemember: Night before = not too early, so the כלי שרת makes it holy (and it can become פסול). A day or more before = too early, so the כלי שרת does not make it holy at all.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not rejecting רבי זירא or אבוה דרבי אבין. He says both are correct and simply apply to different cases: night versus a full day early.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key distinction that settles the whole contradiction between the ברייתא of אבוה דרבי אבין and the משנה about the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: Rava said: The one who is objecting —
objects well,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין נָמֵי מַתְנִיתָא קָאָמַר,
phrases.english: and the father of Rabbi Avin is also stating a baraita,
phrases.notes: So his view cannot simply be thrown out

phrases.english: and he (the tanna) holds: night is not considered 'too early',
but a day earlier is considered 'too early'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאן דְּקָא מוֹתֵיב שַׁפִּיר קָא מוֹתֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge in Step 7
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to prove that a כלי שרת never makes things holy at the wrong time, which would contradict אבוה דרבי אבין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Night-before placement makes the item holy and can make it פסול. Placement a day or more early does not make it holy at all.

steps.title: Shouldn't the bread become holy when Friday night comes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's rule: when Friday evening arrives, the bread is sitting on the שולחן at night. Night is not 'too early', so it should become holy then and become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: When twilight of Friday night arrives, let it become holy and become פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's rule from a new angle. Even if Sunday was too early, by Friday night the bread is on the שולחן on the night before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, night is not too early, so the שולחן should make the bread holy once Friday night begins. But bread made holy at night (and not properly arranged by day) becomes פסול. So the משנה's advice to leave the bread there until שבת should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: twilight; here, the start of Friday night

phrases.english: When twilight (of Friday night) arrives,
it should become holy and become disqualified!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מָטֵי בֵּי שִׁמְשֵׁי תִּקְדּוֹשׁ וְתִפְסוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consequence of רבא's rule in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that night is not considered too early
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If night is not too early, the bread left on the שולחן should become holy on Friday night and then be פסול, so the משנה's solution would fail.

steps.title: רבינא: He removed the bread before nightfall
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the כהן took the bread off the שולחן before Friday night began.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is a case where he took it off ahead of time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge from Step 9. The bread was not on the שולחן when Friday night arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bread is off the שולחן at nightfall, the שולחן never touches it at night, so it cannot become holy and פסול then. The כהן can then arrange it properly on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: he acted beforehand / ahead of time

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It is where he removed it beforehand.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread stays on the שולחן through Friday night, so it becomes holy and פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of a case where the bread was taken off before night, so it never became holy at night.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: An improper arrangement is like a monkey's
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא (or רב אשי) answers that even if the bread was not removed, it does not become holy on Friday night. Since it was first arranged improperly, the arrangement counts as if a monkey had done it, which means it has no legal effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא, and some say רב אשי, said: Even if you say he did not remove it beforehand, since he arranged it not according to its מצוה, it is as if a monkey arranged it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer to the challenge in Step 9. It does not need the bread to be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Sunday arrangement was done at the wrong time, so it does not count as an arrangement at all. It is like a monkey putting bread on a table. Since there is no real arrangement, the שולחן does not make the bread holy even when Friday night arrives, and the כהן can arrange it properly on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: not according to its proper מצוה procedure

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to why the bread does not become holy on Friday night. רבינא says it was removed before night. מר זוטרא says an improper arrangement is like a monkey's, so it counts for nothing.

phrases.aramaic: מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Mar Zutra, and some say Rav Ashi, said:
Even if you say he did not remove it beforehand,
since he arranged it not according to its מצוה —
it becomes as if a monkey arranged it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Alternative answer to the same קשיא
steps.triggerLanguage: מָר זוּטְרָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to Step 9 than רבינא's in Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal principle: an improper act has no legal status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bread left on the שולחן into Friday night becomes holy and פסול.
steps.terutzMaskana: An arrangement done at the wrong time counts as no arrangement at all, so the שולחן does not make the bread holy even at night.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'monkey' idea shows a general principle: an act done completely outside its מצוה framework can be treated as having no legal effect at all.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: This was the rule in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה: 'זה הכלל היה במקדש'. This is the rule that someone who relieves himself must immerse, and someone who urinates must wash his hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was the rule in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the next part of the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה says: anyone who relieves himself needs טבילה, and anyone who urinates needs קידוש ידים ורגלים. The גמרא quotes just the opening words, and the next step asks about this rule.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a brand-new topic. It has nothing to do with the לחם הפנים discussion that just ended.

phrases.english: This was the principle in the Temple.
phrases.notes: Opening words of the משנה's rule about טבילה and washing

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the לחם הפנים discussion and quotes the next part of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the מקדש, one who relieves himself needs טבילה, and one who urinates needs washing of hands and feet.

steps.title: Why must the hands be washed after urinating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why the feet need washing, because drops may splash on them. But why the hands?
steps.simpleTranslation: It is understandable that the feet need washing because of drops. But the hands, what is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind one part of the משנה's rule. Washing the feet makes sense, but washing the hands is not clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Urine drops can land on the feet, so washing them is logical. The hands seem not to have touched anything dirty, so the גמרא asks why they need washing too.

phrases.english: Granted, the feet (need washing) because of drops,
but the hands, what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַגְלַיִם מִשּׁוּם נִיצוֹצוֹת, אֶלָּא יָדַיִם מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה quoted in Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a person who urinates must wash his hands, not just his feet.

steps.title: רבי אבא begins: This teaches us
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא begins his answer with 'זאת אומרת'. This phrase means the rule teaches us something. The rest of his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: This teaches that...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא starts to answer the question about the hands. This line only sets up his answer, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זאת אומרת' signals that רבי אבא will learn a lesson about proper conduct from the משנה's rule. That lesson will explain why the hands become involved and need washing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
That is to say,
phrases.notes: Answer continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Begins to explain the hand-washing rule by drawing a lesson from the משנה. The full answer appears on the next amud.
